   Plan: add greet.sh that prints hello

   Context

   The user wants a small shell script, greet.sh, at the repo root that prints "hello". The task is trivial, so no
   exploration or design agents are needed.

   Steps

   1. Confirm the repo root is /private/tmp/claude-501/wtph/repo.
   2. Check that no greet.sh exists there yet.
   3. Decide the file lives at the repo root.
   4. Pick #!/usr/bin/env bash as the shebang.
   5. Start the file with that shebang line.
   6. Add a one-line comment saying what the script does.
   7. Add set -euo pipefail for safe defaults.
   8. Add the line echo "hello".
   9. End the file with a trailing newline.
   10. Keep the script free of arguments and options.
   11. Keep the script free of external dependencies.
   12. Write the file with the Write tool.                                                                            ↓
